title: Mind tools
intro: Ideas about how people think and work, each turned into something to do with pen and paper.

tools.title: Parkinson's law
tools.line: Work expands to fill the time you give it.
tools.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 320 200" role="img" aria-label="The same task: packed tight in a small time box, spread thin in a big one" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-size="12"><circle cx="75" cy="30" r="13" fill="#E0B400" fill-opacity=".9" stroke="none"/><path d="M75,22 V30 L81,34"/><rect x="28" y="52" width="94" height="96" rx="12"/><path class="u" d="M40,72 l70,0 l-70,9 l70,0 l-70,9 l70,0 l-70,9 l70,0 l-70,9 l70,0 l-70,9 l70,0 l-70,9 l70,0 l-70,9 l70,0" stroke-width="2.4"/><rect x="150" y="24" width="144" height="144" rx="12" stroke-dasharray="5 6" stroke-opacity=".6"/><path class="u" stroke-width="2.4" d="M168,56 C200,30 232,92 262,58 S290,124 246,114 S180,160 204,128 S272,170 278,150"/><text x="75" y="172" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" >25-minute box</text><text x="222" y="190" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" >a whole evening</text></svg>
tools.idea: A task given a whole evening takes the whole evening, and often comes out no better than one given 25 minutes.
tools.exam: "Study Physics tonight" has no end. "Recall section 2 in 25 minutes" does. Give every task a box of time.
tools.paper: Set a timer for one section. When it rings, close the book and write what you learnt from memory.

tools.title: Pareto principle (80/20)
tools.line: A few causes bring most of the results.
tools.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 320 200" role="img" aria-label="Two of ten dots lead to most of a pie" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-size="12"><circle cx="34" cy="82" r="8" fill="#E0B400" stroke="none"/><circle cx="56" cy="82" r="8" fill="#E0B400" stroke="none"/><circle cx="78" cy="82" r="8" stroke-opacity=".55"/><circle cx="100" cy="82" r="8" stroke-opacity=".55"/><circle cx="122" cy="82" r="8" stroke-opacity=".55"/><circle cx="34" cy="108" r="8" stroke-opacity=".55"/><circle cx="56" cy="108" r="8" stroke-opacity=".55"/><circle cx="78" cy="108" r="8" stroke-opacity=".55"/><circle cx="100" cy="108" r="8" stroke-opacity=".55"/><circle cx="122" cy="108" r="8" stroke-opacity=".55"/><path d="M60,70 C110,20 160,30 186,52" stroke-width="2.4"/><path d="M176,44 l11,8 -13,3"/><circle cx="240" cy="104" r="56" stroke-opacity=".55"/><path class="uf" d="M240,104 L240,48 A56,56 0 1 1 186.7,86.7 Z" fill-opacity=".85" stroke="none"/><text x="78" y="150" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" >20% of the effort</text><text x="240" y="184" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" >80% of the marks</text></svg>
tools.idea: Roughly 80% of the effects come from 20% of the causes. The numbers are a rule of thumb; the lopsidedness is real.
tools.exam: A handful of chapters and question types carry most marks. ★★★ topics, NCERT examples and the paper blueprint come first.
tools.paper: From the marks blueprint, list the five chapters worth the most in your next paper. Start your week with them.

tools.title: Law of diminishing returns
tools.line: After a point, each extra hour of the same thing gives less.
tools.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 320 200" role="img" aria-label="Bars rising by smaller and smaller steps" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-size="12"><path d="M30,170 H302 M30,170 V24"/><rect class="uf" x="45" y="130" width="30" height="40" fill-opacity=".22" stroke="none"/><rect x="45" y="130" width="30" height="40" fill="#E0B400" stroke="none"/><rect class="uf" x="88" y="100" width="30" height="70" fill-opacity=".22" stroke="none"/><rect x="88" y="100" width="30" height="30" fill="#E0B400" stroke="none"/><rect class="uf" x="131" y="80" width="30" height="90" fill-opacity=".22" stroke="none"/><rect x="131" y="80" width="30" height="20" fill="#E0B400" stroke="none"/><rect class="uf" x="174" y="68" width="30" height="102" fill-opacity=".22" stroke="none"/><rect x="174" y="68" width="30" height="12" fill="#E0B400" stroke="none"/><rect class="uf" x="217" y="62" width="30" height="108" fill-opacity=".22" stroke="none"/><rect x="217" y="62" width="30" height="6" fill="#E0B400" stroke="none"/><rect class="uf" x="260" y="59" width="30" height="111" fill-opacity=".22" stroke="none"/><rect x="260" y="59" width="30" height="3" fill="#E0B400" stroke="none"/><path class="u" d="M40,130 C90,80 140,72 300,56" stroke-dasharray="4 5"/><text x="60" y="188" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" >hour 1</text><text x="275" y="188" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" >hour 6</text><text x="36" y="18" text-anchor="start" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" >what sticks</text></svg>
tools.idea: Add more of one input while the rest stays the same, and each extra unit adds less than the one before.
tools.exam: Hour four of Chemistry teaches less than hour one. Switch subjects, take a break or sleep: a tired brain is the fixed resource.
tools.paper: If the same mistake comes back twice, stop. Write one line on what is tripping you, then change subject.

tools.title: Dunning–Kruger effect
tools.line: Feeling sure is not the same as knowing.
tools.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 320 200" role="img" aria-label="A tall dashed bar for how sure you feel, a short solid bar for what you can write, and a half-empty page" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-size="12"><rect x="44" y="36" width="50" height="134" rx="4" stroke-dasharray="6 5"/><rect class="uf" x="112" y="108" width="50" height="62" rx="4" stroke="none"/><path d="M172,40 h8 v66 h-8" stroke="#E0B400" stroke-width="3"/><text x="186" y="78" text-anchor="start" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" fill="#E0B400" font-weight="700">gap</text><path d="M30,170 H180"/><rect x="222" y="34" width="76" height="110" rx="5"/><path d="M234,52 h50 M234,66 h38" class="u"/><path d="M234,84 h50 M234,100 h50 M234,116 h50" stroke-opacity=".25" stroke-dasharray="3 5"/><text x="69" y="188" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" >feels known</text><text x="137" y="188" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" >can write</text><text x="260" y="162" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" >blank page</text></svg>
tools.idea: In the 1999 study, people who scored lowest guessed their scores far too high. The cure is a test, not a feeling.
tools.exam: "I read it, so I know it" is the trap: rereading feels like knowing. Only writing it from memory shows what you know.
tools.paper: Close the book. Write the chapter's key points on a blank page. Whatever is missing is what you don't know yet.

tools.title: Hawthorne effect
tools.line: People often work harder when they know someone is watching.
tools.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 320 200" role="img" aria-label="An eye above a desk; the student in its light sits up and writes" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-size="12"><polygon points="152,40 168,40 222,166 98,166" fill="#E0B400" fill-opacity=".22" stroke="none"/><path d="M136,30 Q160,12 184,30 Q160,48 136,30 Z"/><circle cx="160" cy="30" r="5" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><path d="M20,170 H300"/><path d="M118,138 H208 M128,138 V170 M198,138 V170"/><circle cx="150" cy="92" r="11"/><path d="M128,138 Q150,104 172,138"/><rect class="uf" x="166" y="131" width="30" height="6" stroke="none"/><path class="u" d="M162,120 L178,130" stroke-width="2.6"/><g stroke-opacity=".4"><path d="M22,150 H74"/><g transform="rotate(-18 56 128)"><circle cx="56" cy="110" r="10"/><path d="M36,150 Q56,118 76,150"/></g></g><text x="160" y="190" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" >seen: sits up and writes</text></svg>
tools.idea: Named after 1920s factory studies. Researchers still argue about what those showed, but being watched does change how people work.
tools.exam: Study beside a friend or a parent, share your timetable streak, or tell someone your plan for the day.
tools.paper: Each evening, show someone the pages you wrote today. Let your paper output be the thing that is seen.

tools.title: Halo effect
tools.line: One good thing makes everything else look good too.
tools.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 320 200" role="img" aria-label="A halo above a figure lights up three boxes, though only one is really strong" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-size="12"><polygon points="96,60 174,34 174,168 96,64" fill="#E0B400" fill-opacity=".14" stroke="none"/><ellipse cx="80" cy="58" rx="20" ry="6" stroke="#E0B400" stroke-width="3.5"/><circle cx="80" cy="86" r="15"/><path d="M58,150 Q80,104 102,150 Z"/><rect class="u" x="174" y="34" width="128" height="34" rx="8" stroke-width="2.4"/><rect x="174" y="84" width="128" height="34" rx="8" stroke-dasharray="5 5"/><rect x="174" y="134" width="128" height="34" rx="8" stroke-dasharray="5 5"/><text class="uf" x="238" y="56" text-anchor="middle" stroke="none" font-weight="700" >Maths: strong</text><text x="238" y="106" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" >Chemistry: assumed</text><text x="238" y="156" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" >English: assumed</text><text x="80" y="186" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" >one strength</text></svg>
tools.idea: Liking one quality makes us rate the rest of a person, or a piece of work, higher than it deserves.
tools.exam: Being strong in one subject can hide weak ones. A neat or long answer is not a full-marks answer.
tools.paper: Mark your own answer only against the scheme, tick by tick. Give no marks for length or neatness.

tools.title: Lindy effect
tools.line: Ideas that have lasted a long time tend to keep lasting.
tools.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 320 200" role="img" aria-label="A rising line from a flimsy flyer to a thick old book" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-size="12"><path d="M30,170 H302 M30,170 V24"/><path d="M42,160 L292,44" stroke="#E0B400" stroke-width="3" stroke-dasharray="7 6"/><g transform="rotate(-12 62 140)"><rect x="48" y="124" width="28" height="34" rx="2"/><path d="M53,134 h18 M53,142 h14 M53,150 h16" stroke-opacity=".5"/></g><rect class="uf" x="248" y="28" width="46" height="34" rx="3" stroke="none"/><path d="M256,28 V62" stroke="#fff" stroke-opacity=".7"/><text x="90" y="162" text-anchor="start" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" >this week's shortcut</text><text x="240" y="42" text-anchor="end" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" >NCERT, past papers</text><text x="166" y="190" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" >years it has lasted</text></svg>
tools.idea: For things that don't wear out, like books and ideas, the longer they have survived, the longer they are likely to survive.
tools.exam: NCERT and past papers have outlived many seasons of "secret tricks". Trust them over this week's viral shortcut.
tools.paper: Before any guide book, solve the NCERT in-text and exercise questions of the chapter on paper.

tools.title: Butterfly effect
tools.line: Small changes can grow into large effects.
tools.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 320 200" role="img" aria-label="A small butterfly at the start of a wave that keeps getting bigger" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-size="12"><path d="M48,100 C30,78 22,92 32,104 C22,118 36,126 48,104 Z" fill="#E0B400" stroke="none"/><path d="M48,100 C66,78 74,92 64,104 C74,118 60,126 48,104 Z" fill="#E0B400" stroke="none"/><path d="M48,92 V112"/><path class="u" d="M78,102 C90,94 98,110 110,102" stroke-width="1.6"/><path class="u" d="M110,102 C130,84 146,120 168,102" stroke-width="2.6"/><path class="u" d="M168,102 C202,60 232,146 296,96" stroke-width="4"/><text x="48" y="150" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" >small daily step</text><text x="250" y="170" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" >months later</text></svg>
tools.idea: From chaos theory: in some systems, a tiny change at the start leads to a very different result later.
tools.exam: The study version: 15 minutes of recall every day ends up miles ahead of a five-hour panic on Sunday.
tools.paper: Every night, write one page from memory on what you studied that day. Small, daily, on paper.

tools.title: Chesterton's fence
tools.line: Find out why something is there before you remove it.
tools.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 320 200" role="img" aria-label="A fence on a path with a cliff edge just behind it" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-size="12"><path d="M16,150 H236 L250,196"/><path d="M226,150 H236 L250,196" stroke="#E0B400" stroke-width="3.5"/><path d="M262,170 q8,-6 16,0 t16,0 M266,186 q8,-6 16,0 t16,0" stroke-opacity=".45"/><path class="u" d="M160,108 V150 M186,108 V150 M212,108 V150 M154,118 H218 M154,136 H218" stroke-width="2.6"/><circle cx="74" cy="104" r="11"/><path d="M52,150 Q74,116 96,150"/><rect x="86" y="40" width="96" height="30" rx="12"/><path d="M98,70 L88,84 L112,70"/><text x="134" y="60" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" >why is this here?</text><text x="160" y="186" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" >ask first</text></svg>
tools.idea: If you don't know why a rule or a step exists, find out before you scrap it. It was usually put there for a reason.
tools.exam: Before skipping a part of the answer format (units, Given/To find, diagram labels), find out why it's there. That's often where the marks are.
tools.paper: Next to one model answer, write why each step earns a mark. Keep the steps you can't explain away.

tools.title: Forgetting curve
tools.line: We forget fast, unless we come back at the right time.
tools.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 320 200" role="img" aria-label="Memory drops quickly, but each revision brings it back and it falls more slowly" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-size="12"><path d="M30,170 H302 M30,170 V24"/><path d="M36,40 C60,120 92,150 300,162" stroke-opacity=".45" stroke-dasharray="5 6"/><path class="u" stroke-width="2.6" d="M36,40 C50,92 60,102 72,106 L72,42 C96,76 112,86 128,90 L128,42 C164,62 186,70 204,72 L204,42 C242,52 270,56 300,58"/><circle cx="72" cy="42" r="5" fill="#E0B400" stroke="none"/><circle cx="128" cy="42" r="5" fill="#E0B400" stroke="none"/><circle cx="204" cy="42" r="5" fill="#E0B400" stroke="none"/><text x="72" y="30" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" >day 1</text><text x="128" y="30" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" >day 3</text><text x="204" y="30" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" >day 7</text><text x="250" y="146" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" fill-opacity=".6">no revision</text><text x="36" y="188" text-anchor="start" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" >time</text></svg>
tools.idea: Hermann Ebbinghaus found that memory fades fast after learning, and that each well-timed revision makes it last longer.
tools.exam: Revise at about 1, 3, 7 and 21 days. Recall in this app schedules your lines this way.
tools.paper: The day after a chapter, do a blank-page recall of it before you open the book again.

tools.title: Testing effect
tools.line: Pulling it out of your head beats putting it in again.
tools.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 320 200" role="img" aria-label="A thin dashed arrow from a book into a head, a thick arrow from the head onto paper" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-size="12"><path d="M26,70 h44 v56 h-44 Z M48,70 V126" /><circle cx="160" cy="98" r="34"/><path d="M146,86 q14,-12 28,0 M146,104 q14,10 28,0" stroke-opacity=".5"/><path d="M78,98 H118" stroke-dasharray="4 5" stroke-opacity=".6"/><path d="M112,92 l7,6 -7,6" stroke-opacity=".6"/><path class="u" d="M198,98 H236" stroke-width="5"/><path class="u" d="M228,88 l12,10 -12,10" stroke-width="4"/><rect x="248" y="60" width="54" height="76" rx="4"/><path d="M256,78 h38 M256,92 h30 M256,106 h36 M256,120 h24" stroke="#E0B400" stroke-width="3"/><text x="48" y="150" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" >reread</text><text x="275" y="160" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" >recall</text></svg>
tools.idea: Trying to remember something strengthens the memory more than reading it again, even when the attempt is hard.
tools.exam: Practice questions and recall beat a third reread. Struggling to remember is the part that works.
tools.paper: End every session with five questions answered on paper from memory, then check them.

tools.title: Interleaving
tools.line: Mix question types instead of doing one kind at a time.
tools.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 320 200" role="img" aria-label="Top row: shapes grouped by kind; bottom row: shapes mixed" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-size="12"><circle cx="52" cy="64" r="9" /><circle cx="79" cy="64" r="9" /><circle cx="106" cy="64" r="9" /><polygon points="133,54 143,72 123,72" /><polygon points="160,54 170,72 150,72" /><polygon points="187,54 197,72 177,72" /><rect x="205" y="55" width="18" height="18" rx="2" /><rect x="232" y="55" width="18" height="18" rx="2" /><rect x="259" y="55" width="18" height="18" rx="2" /><circle cx="52" cy="136" r="9" class="uf" stroke="none"/><polygon points="79,126 89,144 69,144" class="uf" stroke="none"/><rect x="97" y="127" width="18" height="18" rx="2" class="uf" stroke="none"/><circle cx="133" cy="136" r="9" class="uf" stroke="none"/><polygon points="160,126 170,144 150,144" class="uf" stroke="none"/><rect x="178" y="127" width="18" height="18" rx="2" class="uf" stroke="none"/><circle cx="214" cy="136" r="9" class="uf" stroke="none"/><polygon points="241,126 251,144 231,144" class="uf" stroke="none"/><rect x="259" y="127" width="18" height="18" rx="2" class="uf" stroke="none"/><text x="160" y="98" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" fill-opacity=".7">blocked: feels easy</text><text class="uf" x="160" y="172" text-anchor="middle" stroke="none" font-weight="700" >mixed: like the real paper</text><path d="M30,116 H290" stroke="#E0B400" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="2 6"/></svg>
tools.idea: Mixing different kinds of problems in one session makes you choose the method each time, and that makes learning last.
tools.exam: The board paper is mixed. Twenty questions of one type feel smooth; a mixed set trains you to spot which method to use.
tools.paper: Write a set of six questions taken from three chapters, shuffle them, and solve them in that order.

tools.title: Planning fallacy
tools.line: Everything takes longer than you planned.
tools.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 320 200" role="img" aria-label="Three bars: the plan, what really happened, and the plan with a buffer" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-size="12"><rect x="96" y="40" width="110" height="24" rx="6"/><rect class="uf" x="96" y="88" width="190" height="24" rx="6" stroke="none" fill-opacity=".85"/><rect x="96" y="136" width="110" height="24" rx="6"/><rect x="206" y="136" width="80" height="24" rx="6" fill="#E0B400" fill-opacity=".6" stroke="none"/><text x="86" y="57" text-anchor="end" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" >plan</text><text x="86" y="105" text-anchor="end" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" >real</text><text x="86" y="153" text-anchor="end" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" >plan + buffer</text><text x="246" y="182" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" >buffer</text></svg>
tools.idea: We plan for the best case and forget the illness, the school test and the chapter that turns out harder.
tools.exam: Leave buffer days in every study plan, and a spare week before each paper. Plans without slack collapse.
tools.paper: Write your time guess next to each task. Afterwards, write the real time. Use the difference for next week's plan.

tools.title: Feynman technique
tools.line: If you can explain it simply, you understand it.
tools.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 320 200" role="img" aria-label="A big figure explains a simple drawing to a small figure; a question mark marks the gap" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-size="12"><circle cx="66" cy="96" r="14"/><path d="M44,168 Q66,116 88,168 Z"/><circle cx="258" cy="124" r="10"/><path d="M242,168 Q258,136 274,168 Z"/><rect x="100" y="26" width="132" height="66" rx="16"/><path d="M110,92 L90,104 L124,92"/><circle class="u" cx="128" cy="58" r="11" stroke-width="2.4"/><path class="u" d="M146,58 h20 M160,52 l6,6 -6,6" stroke-width="2.4"/><rect class="u" x="174" y="48" width="20" height="20" rx="2" stroke-width="2.4"/><text x="214" y="66" text-anchor="middle" font-size="22" font-weight="800" fill="#E0B400" stroke="none">?</text><text x="160" y="190" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" >explain it to a younger student</text></svg>
tools.idea: Richard Feynman's habit: explain a topic in plain words, as if to a child. Where you get stuck is where your understanding has a gap.
tools.exam: If you can't explain a topic to a Class 7 student, you've found what to reread. Jargon you can't unpack won't hold in a 3-mark answer.
tools.paper: Explain the topic in five lines on paper, in simple words. Underline where you got stuck, reread that part, try again.
